A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IntLoRA framework. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable, allowing content to be matched across substantial reorganization and revised experiments.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-generation experiments, component ablations and Llama3 mathematical-question-answering results, including Tables 1–6 and appendix case studies.

after.justification: v3 reports original image-generation and NLP results, ablations, training measurements, and an additional ImageNet diffusion-quantization comparison.

M1.justification: v3 extends the implementation to activation quantization, explicitly included in Algorithms 2–3, whereas v1 restricts itself to weight quantization. AQS, MLA, VMC, the low-rank parameterization and the MUL/SHIFT weight-merging formulations otherwise remain substantially unchanged; the added pseudocode mostly documents that existing framework.

E1.justification: v3 adds ImageNet 256×256 generation for evaluating diffusion-model quantization, a limited extension beyond downstream customization (Section 6, Table 6). DreamBooth, ADE20K, CelebA-HQ, COCO, StyleDrop and MetaMathQA/GSM8K remain represented. The smaller DreamBooth subset changes sample coverage within the retained task, rather than introducing a new task.

E2.justification: EfficientDM becomes an evaluated comparator in v3 Table 6, rather than only related work. IR-QLoRA disappears from the aggregate NLP comparison, although its appendix case study remains; QA-LoRA and IR-QLoRA also disappear from the efficiency comparison. The main image-generation comparator set is retained.

E3.justification: DreamBooth evaluation changes from the stated 25 subjects with 30 prompts each to 15 subject–prompt pairs, and from weight-only quantization to W8A8/W4A8. Controllable-generation reporting drops CLIPIQA and NIQE, while style evaluation becomes qualitative only. The efficiency experiment changes from SDXL storage accounting to SD1.5 training measurements. A new W4A4 ImageNet protocol uses LDM-4, 20 DDIM steps and 500 training epochs. These materially revise the evaluation design.

E4.justification: v3 Appendices E–F and Figure 12 add diagnostics examining whether the auxiliary matrix introduces outliers and whether learned AB values are sufficiently smaller than R to justify the approximation. v1's channel-wise weight-range analysis and Figure 11 are removed. The rank, smoothing-factor, distribution-choice and VMC analyses, along with the qualitative case studies, are otherwise retained or relocated.

E5.justification: v3 Section 4.1 newly mentions regenerating the auxiliary matrix using a fixed random seed. This is limited seed-related disclosure: it provides neither a seed value nor repeated-run counts, uncertainty estimates or significance tests, and does not establish that additional experimental runs were performed.

E6.justification: DreamBooth scores are replaced under changed settings, and several controllable-generation FIDs and distribution-ablation scores change. LoRA's reported NLP accuracy changes from 62.24% to 64.24%, placing it above the retained 64.23% IntLoRA-MUL result. v3 adds training measurements and ImageNet results: FID is 10.43 for MUL, 20.20 for SHIFT and 13.42 for EfficientDM. Quantitative style results, CLIPIQA/NIQE results and per-task storage estimates are removed. These are substantial evidence changes, not established same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The main derivations remain, but displayed mathematical reasoning changes locally. Equation (6) replaces correlation with W−R by correlation with Q(W−R), while retaining the same expression for the limit. Equation (5) changes the denominator from Wround−z to W−R without the corresponding scaling adjustment. No new formal proof establishes these revisions; Appendix F supplies empirical support for an existing approximation.

C1.justification: v1 emphasizes efficiency across fine-tuning, per-task storage and inference. v3 centers inference-aware tuning without additional PTQ and explicitly claims significant speedup in both training and inference without performance loss. The central integral-adaptation contribution remains, but the speedup claim becomes more specific and the storage contribution is de-emphasized.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the new distributions as showing that VMC avoids auxiliary-matrix outliers and supports neglecting AB in the approximation. It removes the channel-specific variance rationale and the quantitative discussion of style–content balance. The limitations concerning floating-point training, heuristic auxiliary-matrix selection and restriction to LoRA remain essentially unchanged in Appendix G.

D1.justification: v3 adds preprocessing and forward-pass pseudocode, auxiliary-matrix regeneration information, explicit quantization granularity, RTX 3090 timing hardware and the ImageNet training configuration. Conversely, it removes v1's NLP recipe: AdamW for two epochs, cosine scheduling, 0.005 warm-up ratio, Alpaca zero-shot evaluation and query/value-only LoRA placement. Most image-training hyperparameters and the code-access link are retained. Together these substantially change the reproducibility documentation.

R1.justification: v3 adds FLUX as motivation and develops a substantive distinction from EfficientDM based on loading quantized versus floating-point weights during training. It removes v1's dedicated QA-LoRA comparison and discussions of OFT, butterfly orthogonal fine-tuning and PTQD. The broader positioning at the intersection of LoRA and quantization remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, preliminaries and related work are extensively rewritten or condensed. Efficiency receives a separate subsection, NLP evaluation moves into the main Further Discussion section, and the variance-distribution discussion moves to an appendix. The appendices are substantially reorganized around algorithms and diagnostics, beyond simple renumbering.

P2.justification: The single-column preprint becomes a two-column conference paper. The opening composite figure is split, the method diagram is redrawn, and benchmark tables are substantially restructured. The quantitative style table and channel-wise weight-range figure are removed; algorithm boxes, an ImageNet table and auxiliary-weight distribution plots are added. Most qualitative image grids retain their content while being resized and relocated.

improvement.justification: v3 adds useful algorithms, auxiliary-matrix diagnostics and an EfficientDM benchmark, but reduces the stated DreamBooth evaluation and removes quantitative style evidence, controllability metrics and the NLP training recipe. Its stronger speedup claim also lacks clear support: Table 3 reports 0.84–0.87 seconds per image for IntLoRA versus 0.68 for LoRA, and provides no inference latency. These gains and losses leave the net quality direction uncertain.
